purpose: Melody-turning feasibility probe (Kim direct 2026-07-22): impose a per-frame chroma target stream (exact, from frame-locked test MIDIs) through LatCH target_raw guidance — free-gen melody adoption (arm A) and SDEdit a2a melody TURNING pat1->pat2/pat6 (arm B) vs unguided SDEdit control (arm C).
hypothesis: If training-free frame-level chroma steering has real per-frame pitch authority (not just static-key authority), arm B outputs keep the source texture but adopt the target melody: target-adoption high, source-retention low, disintegration gate clean. Bears directly on Head B's role.
dataset_info: no training — pretrained SA3 medium-base + shipped LatCH chroma heads

gain_extension.verdict: CLOSED — dose-response flat to g8192 on 3/4 target-seed combos (adoption == null); single riser (pat6/s5678 0.28-0.34 vs null 0.11) keeps source retention 0.78 = not a turn; first gate failures of the run appear at g4096 (zcr, seed 5678 both targets) and g8192 degrades transcription coverage 0.98->0.82. Quality does NOT survive to 8192 for same_chroma, contra the 07-19 scalar-head finding.

result.verdict: NEGATIVE — training-free frame-level chroma steering does not turn melodies at gains 1536-2048. Arm B (SDEdit a2a) steered target-adoption equals the unguided control (0.172 vs 0.172 pat2 nl0.6; 0.0 vs 0.0 pat6); arm A free-gen adoption lifts are seed-idiosyncratic, chroma delta <= +0.02. All 26 base clips gate-clean. Head B's bar stands; this probe's frame-locked adoption/retention/gate harness is its acceptance instrument. Details: REPORT.md
